spelling: a squeeze deep in the throat
Gulf speakers say q as a hard g
some Emirati words turn k into ch
a tiny catch in the throat
long vowels: hold them a little longer

modules.title: Greetings and courtesy
modules.blurb: Say hello, ask how someone is, thank people and get by when you don't understand.

items.note: Very Emirati. To a woman: 7ayyaach allah.

items.en: God greet you too (reply to welcome)
Please, go ahead / here you are (to a man)
God give you strength (to someone working)
Do you speak English? (to a man)

modules.title: Numbers, money and time
modules.blurb: Count, ask prices, talk about times and days.

items.en: Do you have time? (to a man)

modules.title: Me, family and work
modules.blurb: Introduce yourself, talk about where you're from, your work and your family.

items.en: Where are you from? (to a man)

items.note: Emirati turns j into y: jooaan becomes yoo3aan.

items.en: Do you have children? (to a man)

modules.title: Getting around Dubai
modules.blurb: Taxis, directions, the café and the shop.

items.en: Where are you going? (to a man)
What would you like? (to a man)
What do you want to eat? (to a man)

items.note: In the Gulf 3aish means rice, not bread.
safari means takeaway in the Gulf.

items.en: What do you recommend? (to a man)

items.note: Shake the little cup gently when you've had enough.
Emirati k becomes ch: kabeer becomes chibeer.

items.en: Can you go a bit lower?

items.note: Emirati j becomes y; many Gulf speakers say jadeed.

items.en: Are you free tomorrow? (to a man)

items.note: Borrowed from English, used all over Dubai.

items.en: Call me back / reply to me

items.note: In Dubai offices people often just say deadline.

items.en: What do you think? (to a man)
Did you send it? (to a man)
Let me check and get back to you

items.note: Gulf way to say well done.

modules.blurb: Repairs, deliveries, the building guard and neighbours.

items.en: Can you help me? (to a man)

modules.blurb: Feeling unwell, the pharmacy, asking for help.

items.en: What did you do? (to a man)
items.note: sawwa (to do) is one of the most useful Gulf verbs.

items.en: May you see it again (Eid reply)

modules.title: Telling stories
modules.blurb: Past events, plans and connecting ideas.

items.note: The plural sawaalif gives this app its name.
In the Gulf gi3ad means to wake up.

items.en: I've been in Dubai for ... years

dialogues.title: Morning at the office
dialogues.setting: Your colleague Mariam greets you as you arrive.

lines.en: Peace be upon you, good morning!
And upon you peace, good morning.
How are you? How are things?
Good, thank God. And you?

lines.ar: الحمد لله. يلا، عندنا اجتماع الحين.
lines.en: Thank God. Come on, we have a meeting now.
Yes, let's go.

questions.q: What do you both have now?

dialogues.title: Meeting someone new
dialogues.setting: At a business event, Noura introduces herself.

lines.en: Hi there! What's your name?
My name is Pranjal. And you?

lines.tr: ana Noura. tsharrafna. inta min wain?
lines.ar: أنا نورة. تشرفنا. إنت من وين؟
lines.en: I'm Noura. Nice to meet you. Where are you from?

lines.tr: ana min il-hind, bas askun fi dbai.
lines.ar: أنا من الهند، بس أسكن في دبي.
lines.en: I'm from India, but I live in Dubai.
Wonderful! Do you speak Arabic?
A little. I'm learning.
Very good!

questions.q: Where are you from, according to the conversation?
How much Arabic do you say you speak?

dialogues.title: Karak at the cafeteria
dialogues.setting: You order at a roadside cafeteria.

lines.en: Hi, what would you like?
I'd like a karak tea, please.
With sugar or without?
Without sugar. And water too.
Here you are.
How much?
Five dirhams.
Thanks.

questions.q: How do you want your tea?

dialogues.title: Asking the price
dialogues.setting: You like a bag at a shop in the souk.

lines.en: Excuse me, how much is this?
This is two hundred dirhams.
Too expensive! Is there a discount?
For you, a hundred and fifty.
OK, done.

questions.q: What price do you agree on?

dialogues.title: Taxi to the Marina
dialogues.setting: You get into a taxi on Sheikh Zayed Road.

lines.en: Peace be upon you. Where are you going?

lines.tr: wa 3alaikum as-salaam. dbai marina, law sama7t.
lines.ar: وعليكم السلام. دبي مارينا، لو سمحت.
lines.en: And upon you peace. Dubai Marina, please.
I'm in a bit of a hurry. Is there traffic?
No, there's no traffic now.
At the traffic light, turn right.
Stop here, please.
There you go.

questions.q: Where should the driver turn right?

dialogues.title: Setting a meeting
dialogues.setting: A colleague wants to meet tomorrow.

lines.en: Do you have time tomorrow?
Yes, in the morning.
Is ten o'clock good?

lines.ar: لا، عندي اجتماع الساعة عشر. الساعة إحدعش؟
lines.en: No, I have a meeting at ten. Eleven o'clock?

lines.tr: zain, ittafagna. is-saa3a i7da3sh fil maktab.
lines.ar: زين، اتفقنا. الساعة إحدعش في المكتب.
lines.en: OK, agreed. Eleven o'clock at the office.
God willing.

questions.q: When do you agree to meet?

dialogues.title: Lunch with a colleague
dialogues.setting: Your colleague Huda suggests lunch near the office.

lines.en: Let's have lunch. What do you want to eat?
I'd like rice and chicken. And you?
I'd like fish and salad.
Is this spicy?
No, it's not spicy. Enjoy!
Really tasty! The bill's on me.

lines.tr: la, mashkoor. khallni adfa3 il-marra il-jaaya.
lines.ar: لا، مشكور. خلني أدفع المرة الجاية.
lines.en: No, thanks. Let me pay next time.

questions.q: Who says they'll pay this time?

dialogues.title: Takeaway order
dialogues.setting: You stop at a cafeteria on the way home.

lines.en: Hi! For here or takeaway?

lines.tr: safari, law sama7t. abi khubz w 3aseer.
lines.ar: سفري، لو سمحت. أبي خبز وعصير.
lines.en: Takeaway, please. I'd like bread and juice.
Cold juice?

lines.tr: ee, baarid. w zeed shway khubz.
lines.en: Yes, cold. And add a bit more bread.
OK. Twenty dirhams.
Here you go. Keep the change.

questions.q: Is the order for here or takeaway?

dialogues.title: Perfume at the souk
dialogues.setting: You're looking for oud at a perfume shop in Deira.

lines.en: Welcome! What are you looking for?
I'd like oud oil. Can I smell it?
Of course, go ahead. This one is new.
Very nice. How much?
Five hundred dirhams.
Too expensive! What's your last price?
For you, four hundred, and incense as a gift.
OK, I'll take it.

questions.q: What do you get as a gift?

dialogues.title: Exchanging a shirt
dialogues.setting: A shirt you bought doesn't fit, so you go back to the mall.

lines.tr: law sama7t, abi abaddil haadha. mub 3ala magaasi.
lines.ar: لو سمحت، أبي أبدل هذا. مب على مقاسي.
lines.en: Excuse me, I want to exchange this. It doesn't fit me.
Too big or too small?
Much too big. Do you have a smaller one?

lines.tr: ee, bas bloon azrag. ma fi abyadh.
lines.ar: إي، بس بلون أزرق. ما في أبيض.
lines.en: Yes, but in blue. There's no white.
No problem, blue is fine.

dialogues.title: Running late
dialogues.setting: Your friend Shamma calls while you're stuck in traffic.

lines.en: Hello? Where are you?

lines.tr: ana fi it-tareeg. fi za7ma wayid.
lines.ar: أنا في الطريق. في زحمة وايد.
lines.en: I'm on my way. There's a lot of traffic.
When will you arrive?
In ten minutes. I'm late, sorry.
No problem. Send me your location.
OK, I'll send it now.

questions.q: What does Shamma ask you to send?

dialogues.title: Weekend plans
dialogues.setting: Arranging to meet a friend at the weekend.

lines.en: Are you free at the weekend?

lines.tr: yimkin. il-yoom ma 3indi wagt, bas baachir faadhi.
lines.ar: يمكن. اليوم ما عندي وقت، بس باجر فاضي.
lines.en: Maybe. Today I don't have time, but tomorrow I'm free.
Great! Let's meet tomorrow.
Where shall we meet? And what time?
At the mall, at seven.
Sure. See you tomorrow!

dialogues.title: Project check-in
dialogues.setting: A quick call with your manager about a report.

lines.en: When will the report be finished?
I've finished half. I'll send it tomorrow.
It's urgent. The client wants it today.
OK, let me check and get back to you.
Thanks for your effort.

questions.q: How much of the report is done?

dialogues.title: Signing the contract
dialogues.setting: A meeting with a supplier to close a deal.

lines.en: Here's the contract. What do you think?

lines.tr: zain, bas fi mushkila fil taklifa.
lines.ar: زين، بس في مشكلة في التكلفة.
lines.en: Good, but there's a problem with the cost.
We can go down a little.
Good idea. I agree.

lines.tr: zain, waggi3 hni law sama7t. mabrook!
lines.ar: زين، وقع هني لو سمحت. مبروك!
lines.en: OK, sign here please. Congratulations!
Thank you. Good luck!

questions.q: What do you do at the end?

dialogues.title: The AC is broken
dialogues.setting: You call building maintenance on a hot afternoon.

lines.en: Hello, maintenance. Go ahead.
The AC is broken, and it's very hot.
Which floor? And the apartment number?

lines.tr: it-taabig il-khaamis, shagga khams imya w waa7id.
lines.ar: الطابق الخامس، شقة خمس مية وواحد.
lines.en: The fifth floor, apartment 501.
OK, I'm coming in half an hour.
Thanks. The door is open.

dialogues.title: A delivery at the door
dialogues.setting: A courier calls from downstairs.

lines.en: Peace be upon you. I have a parcel for you.
And upon you peace. I'm upstairs, come up.
The lift is broken.
Sorry about that. Leave it with the guard downstairs.
OK, no problem.

questions.q: Why can't the courier come up easily?
Where should he leave the parcel?

dialogues.title: At the pharmacy
dialogues.setting: You have a headache and a fever.

lines.en: Hi, what's wrong?
My head hurts, and I have a fever.
Are you allergic to any medicine?
No, I'm not.

lines.tr: haadhi 7boob. marratain fil yoom, ba3d il-akil.
lines.ar: هذي حبوب. مرتين في اليوم، بعد الأكل.
lines.en: These are pills. Twice a day, after food.
And you need rest. Get well soon!
Thank you (God keep you safe).

questions.q: How often should you take the pills?

dialogues.title: A colleague isn't well
dialogues.setting: Your colleague Aisha looks pale at the office.

lines.en: Are you OK? How are things?
No, I'm sick. My stomach hurts.
Do you need a doctor? There's a clinic nearby.
No, it's fine. I'll go home and rest.
OK. Get well soon!

questions.q: What does she decide to do?

dialogues.title: Monday small talk
dialogues.setting: Coffee with a colleague after the weekend.

lines.en: How was the weekend? What did you do?

lines.tr: kaan zain. ri7t il-ba7ar ma3a rab3i.
lines.ar: كان زين. رحت البحر مع ربعي.
lines.en: It was good. I went to the beach with friends.
Really? It's so hot!

lines.tr: ee, w ir-rtooba wayid. bas kaan 7ilu.
lines.ar: إي، والرطوبة وايد. بس كان حلو.
lines.en: Yes, and very humid. But it was nice.

lines.tr: ana ma sawwait shay. kint ta3baana.
lines.ar: أنا ما سويت شي. كنت تعبانة.
lines.en: I didn't do anything. I was tired.

dialogues.title: Eid greetings
dialogues.setting: You meet your neighbour on the first day of Eid.

lines.en: Eid Mubarak!

lines.ar: عساكم من عواده! من زمان، وينك؟
lines.en: May you see it again! It's been ages, where have you been?
I was travelling. I came back last night.
Welcome! Please, some coffee?
Thank you, with pleasure.

dialogues.title: What happened yesterday?
dialogues.setting: A friend wants to know why you missed dinner.

lines.en: You didn't come last night! What happened?
Long story. First, my battery died.

lines.tr: w ba3dain, fij'a, il-mukayyif kharab fil sayyaara.
lines.ar: وبعدين، فجأة، المكيف خرب في السيارة.
lines.en: And then, suddenly, the AC broke in the car.
Really? And then?

lines.tr: fil aakhir ri7t il-bait w nimt, 3ashaan kint ta3baan.
lines.ar: في الآخر رحت البيت ونمت، عشان كنت تعبان.
lines.en: In the end I went home and slept, because I was tired.

questions.q: Why did you go to sleep?

dialogues.title: Plans for next year
dialogues.setting: Chatting with a colleague about the future.

lines.en: Have you been in Dubai long?

lines.tr: ee, saar li fi dbai sanawaat.
lines.ar: إي، صار لي في دبي سنوات.
lines.en: Yes, I've been in Dubai for years.
And what are you planning next year?

lines.tr: ana naawi at3allam 3arabi zain, 3ashaan atkallam ma3a il-3umala.
lines.ar: أنا ناوي أتعلم عربي زين، عشان أتكلم مع العملاء.
lines.en: I'm planning to learn Arabic well, so I can talk with clients.
Wonderful! Good luck.

questions.q: How long have you been in Dubai?

Ask and answer follow-up questions about family, work and home
Catch the main point of short, clear messages
Keep a short social chat going with help

milestones.name: Everyday conversation
cando: Join a conversation unprepared on familiar topics
Follow clear speech at near-normal speed
Talk about past events and future plans
Deal with most everyday situations in Arabic

Follow group conversations with some gaps
